newsitem.title: USA: NAACP reiterates support for integration.
newsitem.headline: NAACP reiterates support for integration.

text.p: NAACP President Kweisi Mfume reiterated Tuesday the civil rights group's support for integration, but said busing of students was only one way to achieve racially mixed schools.

Mfume made his comments in a statement responding to a New York Times article Monday suggesting the National Association for the Advancement of Coloured People was reviewing its longstanding support for public school integration.
The article said the subject of school integration would be debated at the organisation's annual convention in Pittsburgh in July.
"The NAACP stands by its founding proposition of a single, fully integrated society, for all of America," Mfume said.
"We can still support integrative policies while at the same time (be) fighting to guarantee educational equality for students within our existing public schools," he said.
He said any discussion of forced school busing did not change the aims of the organisation.
"Busing is but one of several tools that can be used to achieve the goal of desegregation of our public schools," he said.
Other means of achieving integration included housing policy, new school construction, magnet schools and programmes for gifted and talented students, he said.
